get.summary:
Lists organization resources that are visible to the user and satisfy
the specified filter.
get.description:
This will only return organizations on which the user has the permission
`resourcemanager.organizations.get`

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description:
Optional. The maximum number of organizations to return in the response.
The server can return fewer organizations than requested. If unspecified,
server picks an appropriate default.

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description:
Optional. A pagination token returned from a previous call to
`ListOrganizations` that indicates from where listing should continue.

parameters.name: showDeleted
parameters.description:
Optional. Controls whether organizations in the DELETE_REQUESTED state
should be returned. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
Optional. An expression for filtering the results of the request.
Filter rules are case insensitive. Filterable fields:

+ `displayName`
+ `state`
+ `createTime` (supports comparison operators)

Examples:

+ `displayName = "Acme Corp"` — exact match on display name.
+ `state = ACTIVE` — only active organizations.
+ `createTime > "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"` — created after date.

For more information, see [AIP-160](https://aip.dev/160).

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description:
Optional. A comma-separated list of fields to order by. The default
order is ascending. Use "desc" after a field name for descending.
Supported fields:

+ `displayName`
+ `createTime`
+ `name`

Example: `createTime desc, displayName`

If not specified, the results are ordered by `name` ascending.

parameters.name: organization
parameters.description: Required. The Organization to create.

parameters.name: organizationId
parameters.description:
Optional. A unique identifier for the organization. If not provided, the
server will generate one. Must start with a letter, contain only lowercase
letters, digits, and hyphens, and be between 4 and 20 characters long.

parameters.name: validateOnly
parameters.description:
Optional. If set to true, the request will only validate the request
without persisting it.

get.summary: Fetches an organization resource identified by the specified resource name.

delete.summary:
Soft-deletes an organization. The org transitions to
`DELETE_REQUESTED` state with `delete_time` set; `purge_time` is
populated to `delete_time + 30 days`. Until purge, the org is
recoverable via `UndeleteOrganization` and remains visible to
`ListOrganizations` callers who pass `show_deleted=true`. After
purge, all data cascades and the slug is freed.
delete.description:
If `force=true`, the 30-day grace window is skipped: the LRO
synchronously cascades all child data and frees the slug.
The org is unrecoverable.

The caller must hold the `owner` role on the organization;
otherwise the LRO completes with PERMISSION_DENIED. The LRO
surfaces cascade progress via `DeleteOrganizationMetadata.Phase`.

parameters.name: etag
parameters.description:
Optional. The etag known to the client for the expected state of
the organization. Used for optimistic concurrency control.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description:
Optional. If true, bypasses the 30-day grace window: the LRO
synchronously cascades all child data (spaces, members, assets,
SSO config, invitations, …) and frees the slug. The org is
unrecoverable. Defaults to false (soft-delete with grace).

patch.summary:
Updates an organization resource. Only the `display_name` and
`annotations` fields can be updated. Use the field mask to specify which
fields to update. Omitting the field mask updates all mutable fields.
patch.description:
The caller must have `resourcemanager.organizations.update` permission
on the specified organization.

parameters.name: organization
parameters.description:
Required. The new definition of the organization. The `name` field must
be populated to identify the organization to update.

displayName.description:
Output only. A human-readable string that refers to the organization in the
Pivox Console. This string is set by the server and cannot be
changed. The string will be set to the primary domain (for example,
"acme.com") of the customer that owns the organization.

state.description: Output only. The organization's current lifecycle state.

createdBy.description: Output only. The identity that created this organization.

createTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when the Organization was created.

updatedBy.description: Output only. The identity that last modified this organization.

updateTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when the Organization was last modified.

deletedBy.description: Output only. The identity that requested deletion of this organization.

deleteTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when the Organization was requested for deletion.

purgeTime.description:
Output only. The time at which this organization will be purged.
Approximately 30 days after deletion.

etag.description:
Output only. A checksum computed by the server based on the current value
of the Organization resource. This may be sent on update and delete
requests to ensure the client has an up-to-date value before proceeding.

annotations.description:
Optional. Labels associated with this organization.
Labels are key-value pairs that can be used to organize and track resources.

Required. The new definition of the organization. The `name` field must
be populated to identify the organization to update.

parameters.description:

get.summary:
Lists the domains claimed by an organization, including those
still pending verification.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Optional. Maximum number of domains to return.

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description: Optional. Page token from a previous ListDomains call.

post.summary:
Claims a DNS domain on behalf of the organization. The server
generates a verification token (returned in the LRO metadata),
creates a `Domain` row with `state=PENDING`, and starts polling
DNS for the TXT record at `_pivox-verify.<domain>`. The LRO
completes when the record is observed (state → VERIFIED) or
when the grace window elapses (state → FAILED, phase=EXPIRED).
post.description:
The verification token lives in the LRO metadata and is
available immediately on operation creation — clients display
DNS-record instructions without waiting for the LRO to finish.

The caller must hold a role on the organization that grants
`resourcemanager.domains.create`. Returns ALREADY_EXISTS if the
domain is already claimed by any organization (the response
does not disclose which org).

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description:
Required. The Domain to create. The `domain` field must be set;
all other fields are output-only.

parameters.name: domainId
parameters.description:
Optional. The id portion of the resource name. If unset, the
server uses the lowercase form of `domain.domain`. If set, must
equal that value (provided for AIP-133 compliance and idempotent
retries).

get.summary: Fetches a single domain by resource name.

delete.summary:
Releases a domain claim. Cancels the in-flight `CreateDomain`
LRO if still running. Returns FAILED_PRECONDITION if the
domain is the last `VERIFIED` domain on an `enabled=true`
SsoConfig (admins must disable SSO or add another verified
domain first).

parameters.name: etag
parameters.description:
Optional. The etag known to the client. Used for optimistic
concurrency control.

SsoConfig singleton at `organizations/{org}/ssoConfig`. If no
config has been set, returns NOT_FOUND.

Updates the SSO configuration for an organization (AIP-156
singleton sub-resource). The server applies changes by calling
Firebase Admin SDK to update the underlying provider config,
then persists the local SsoConfig row. `client_secret` (when
provided) is encrypted at rest via Cloud KMS before storage.

parameters.name: ssoConfig
parameters.description:
Required. The new definition of the SsoConfig. The `name` field

Output only. The Firebase Auth provider id. Server-managed; the
server creates / updates the underlying Firebase provider config
when this SsoConfig is updated. Format: `oidc.<slug>` for OIDC,
`saml.<slug>` for SAML.

Required. Human-readable display name shown on the sign-in

Optional. Whether SSO is currently active. When `false`, the
SsoConfig remains stored but `auth:resolveProvider` returns
NOT_FOUND for the org's domains and no Firebase provider is
exposed.

OIDC provider configuration. Set when the IDP supports OAuth

saml.description:

post.summary:
Returns the subset of requested permissions the caller is allowed
on the organization. UI clients use this to gate buttons and
menus. Empty list (not an error) for callers with no role
bindings on the org.

Atomically promotes a user to `owner` and demotes the previous
sole owner to `admin` of the organization. Both updates run in a
single transaction so the org never has zero owners. Returns
FAILED_PRECONDITION when the org already has multiple owners
(use UpdateMember + CreateMember instead) or when the new owner
is already an owner.

Restores a soft-deleted organization (`DELETE_REQUESTED` state)
back to `ACTIVE`, clearing `delete_time` and `purge_time`. Only
callable during the 30-day grace window before purge. After
purge there is no way back.

idToken.description:
Optional. Implicit flow with id_token only. No `client_secret`
needed.

name.description:
The server-assigned name, which is only unique within the same service that
originally returns it. If you use the default HTTP mapping, the
`name` should be a resource name ending with `operations/{unique_id}`.

metadata.description:
Service-specific metadata associated with the operation.  It typically
contains progress information and common metadata such as create time.
Some services might not provide such metadata.  Any method that returns a
long-running operation should document the metadata type, if any.

done.description:
If the value is `false`, it means the operation is still in progress.
If `true`, the operation is completed, and either `error` or `response` is
available.

error.description: The error result of the operation in case of failure or cancellation.

response.description:
The normal, successful response of the operation.  If the original
method returns no data on success, such as `Delete`, the response is
`google.protobuf.Empty`.  If the original method is standard
`Get`/`Create`/`Update`, the response should be the resource.  For other
methods, the response should have the type `XxxResponse`, where `Xxx`
is the original method name.  For example, if the original method name
is `TakeSnapshot()`, the inferred response type is
`TakeSnapshotResponse`.

longrunningOperation.description:
This resource represents a long-running operation that is the result of a
network API call.

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com. As of May 2023, there are no widely used type server
implementations and no plans to implement one.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

code.description:
The status code, which should be an enum value of
[google.rpc.Code][google.rpc.Code].

message.description:
A developer-facing error message, which should be in English. Any
user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the
[google.rpc.Status.details][google.rpc.Status.details] field, or localized
by the client.

details.description:
A list of messages that carry the error details.  There is a common set of
message types for APIs to use.

rpcStatus.description:
The `Status` type defines a logical error model that is suitable for
different programming environments, including REST APIs and RPC APIs. It is
used by [gRPC](https://github.com/grpc). Each `Status` message contains
three pieces of data: error code, error message, and error details.

You can find out more about this error model and how to work with it in the
[API Design Guide](https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors).

id.description:
The identity's stable UUID (firebase_identities.id). Always
populated when the column is non-null in the database, even for
soft-deleted identities.

displayName.description: Resolved display name. Empty for soft-deleted identities.

email.description: Resolved email address. Empty for soft-deleted identities.

isDeleted.description:
True when the identity has been soft-deleted. PII fields are
blanked out in that case while id is preserved.

typesActor.description:
Actor is a resolved reference to an identity. It is used flat on
resources to expose audit fields (created_by, updated_by, deleted_by)
per AIP-148, and can be reused at non-audit positions like assignee
or approver.

Actor lives in `pivox.types` (unversioned — type definitions are
shared infrastructure, not an API surface) so every domain package
(pivox.api.v1, pivox.ai.v1, pivox.assets.v1, pivox.iam.v1,
pivox.storage.v1) can reference it without crossing into a peer
domain — the api-linter's foreign-type-reference rule (AIP-215)
considers `pivox.types` a shared types namespace.

Resolution is performed server-side via the audit.Resolver, which
batches lookups against firebase_identities and caches recent
results. When the underlying identity is soft-deleted the resolver
blanks out PII (display_name, email) and sets is_deleted=true while
preserving the id so that historical references remain stable.

name.description:
Output only. The resource name of the Domain. Format:
`organizations/{organization}/domains/{domain}`. The trailing
segment is the domain name itself (lowercase canonical form).

domain.description:
Required on Create. The fully qualified domain name. Stored
lowercase; case-insensitive on read.

state.description: Output only. Last known verification state.

verifiedTime.description:
Output only. Timestamp when the domain transitioned to
`VERIFIED`, or unset if it has never verified successfully.

createdBy.description: Output only. The identity that registered this domain.

createTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when the Domain row was created.

updatedBy.description: Output only. The identity that last modified this domain.

updateTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when the Domain was last modified.

etag.description:
Output only. A checksum computed by the server based on the
current value of the Domain resource.

v1Domain.description:
Domain is an organization-scoped resource representing a DNS domain
the organization claims to own. Ownership is proved by publishing a
TXT record matching the server-issued `verification_token`; the
`CreateDomain` LRO drives that proof end-to-end.

Domain is decoupled from any single consumer — SSO is the first
caller (a verified domain routes to the org's enabled SsoConfig),
but future features (email allowlist, custom invitation domains,
branding) consume the same resource.

v1DomainState.description:
Verification lifecycle states. A Domain reflects the *last known*
verification result; the active LRO progress lives in
`CreateDomainMetadata.Phase` until it completes.

 - STATE_UNSPECIFIED: Default; not used.
 - PENDING: Domain row exists; verification has not yet succeeded. The
associated `CreateDomain` LRO is either in flight or expired.
 - VERIFIED: The DNS TXT record was observed and matches the issued
`verification_token`. The domain participates in
`auth:resolveProvider` lookups (and any other consumers).
 - FAILED: Verification failed unrecoverably (e.g. token mismatch
detected after a previous VERIFIED state, or the LRO expired
without a successful check). Caller can retry via a fresh
`CreateDomain` cycle (delete + recreate).

allowedDomains.description:

The invitation policy for an organization. Controls which email
addresses can be invited to join the organization.

v1InvitationState.description:
Invitation lifecycle states.

 - STATE_UNSPECIFIED: Unspecified state.
 - PENDING: The invitation is pending acceptance.
 - ACCEPTED: The invitation has been accepted and a user membership was created.
 - DECLINED: The invitation was declined by the recipient.
 - REVOKED: The invitation was revoked by an org admin.
 - EXPIRED: The invitation expired before being accepted or declined.

The resource name of the member.
Format: `organizations/{organization}/members/{member}` or

where `{member}` is `user-{user_id}` or `group-{group_id}`.

v1Member.description:
Multi-parent: a Member lives under either an organization or a space.
The URL segment `{member}` encodes the principal as `user-{user_id}`
or `group-{group_id}` — uniqueness by construction means a given
principal can hold at most one role per scope.

Permission resolution unions org-level and space-level Member
bindings: an org owner is implicitly a space owner. Server-side
resolver is the source of truth; this proto defines only the wire
shape.
v1Member.title:
A Member binds a principal (user or group) to a role at a scope
(organization or space). The single source of truth for "who has
what role where."

issuer.description:
Required. The IDP issuer URL. Must support OIDC discovery at
`<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration`. Example:
`https://accounts.google.com` or
`https://example.okta.com/oauth2/default`.

clientId.description:
Required. The OAuth 2.0 client ID registered with the IDP for
this Pivox organization.

clientSecret.description:
Optional on read; the server returns this field empty (the actual
value is encrypted at rest and never returned to clients). Set on
Update via the `update_mask`. Only required when using the
authorization-code flow (response_type.code = true).

Travels cleartext over TLS to the server, which envelope-encrypts
it via Cloud KMS before persisting.

responseType.description:
Required. The OIDC response type the IDP returns to Firebase
Auth's callback. Most production setups use `code` (authorization-
code flow with `client_secret`). `id_token` is the implicit flow
and does not require a secret.

v1OidcConfig.description:
OIDC provider configuration. Maps onto Firebase Admin SDK's
`OIDCProviderConfig` shape — server reads these fields and calls
`CreateOIDCProviderConfig` / `UpdateOIDCProviderConfig` against
Firebase Auth on Update.

name.description:
Output only. The resource name of the organization. This is the
organization's relative path in the API. Its format is
"organizations/[organization_id]". For example, "organizations/1234".

displayName.description:
Output only. A human-readable string that refers to the organization in the
Pivox Console. This string is set by the server and cannot be
changed. The string will be set to the primary domain (for example,
"acme.com") of the customer that owns the organization.

state.description: Output only. The organization's current lifecycle state.

createdBy.description: Output only. The identity that created this organization.

createTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when the Organization was created.

updatedBy.description: Output only. The identity that last modified this organization.

updateTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when the Organization was last modified.

deletedBy.description: Output only. The identity that requested deletion of this organization.

deleteTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when the Organization was requested for deletion.

purgeTime.description:
Output only. The time at which this organization will be purged.
Approximately 30 days after deletion.

etag.description:
Output only. A checksum computed by the server based on the current value
of the Organization resource. This may be sent on update and delete
requests to ensure the client has an up-to-date value before proceeding.

annotations.description:
Optional. Labels associated with this organization.
Labels are key-value pairs that can be used to organize and track resources.

v1Organization.description:
The root node in the resource hierarchy to which a particular entity's
(a company, for example) resources belong.

v1OrganizationState.description:
Organization lifecycle states.

 - STATE_UNSPECIFIED: Unspecified state.  This is only useful for distinguishing unset values.
 - ACTIVE: The normal and active state.
 - DELETE_REQUESTED: The organization has been marked for deletion by the user.

permissions.description:
Required. The permissions to check. Each entry is a permission ID
(e.g. `spaces.create`, `assets.assets.list`). Wildcards are not
supported.

v1OrganizationsTestIamPermissionsBody.description:
Request message for `Iam.TestIamPermissions`.

Used by clients (notably UI layers) to ask the server: "out of this
list of permissions, which ones does the caller actually have on
this resource?" The server resolves the caller's effective role at
the resource and returns the subset of requested permissions that
role grants.

idpEntityId.description:
Required. The IDP entity ID. Found in the IDP's SAML metadata
under the root `EntityDescriptor[entityID]` attribute.

ssoUrl.description:
Required. The IDP's single-sign-on URL. Found in the IDP's SAML
metadata under `SingleSignOnService[Binding=HTTP-POST].Location`.

x509Certificates.description:
Required. PEM-encoded X.509 certificates the IDP uses to sign
SAML responses. At least one is required; multiple may be
provided during cert rotation.

requestSigningEnabled.description:
Optional. Whether the IDP requires the SP (Pivox/Firebase) to
sign AuthnRequests. Set this to match the IDP's
`WantAuthnRequestsSigned` metadata flag.

rpEntityId.description:
Output only. The relying-party entity ID Pivox uses with this
IDP. Server-derived from the org's resource name; configure your
IDP to expect this value.

callbackUrl.description:
Output only. The Pivox/Firebase callback URL (ACS endpoint) the
IDP should redirect to after authentication. Server-derived from
the Firebase Auth project's hosted handler.

v1SamlConfig.description:
SAML provider configuration. Maps onto Firebase Admin SDK's
`SAMLProviderConfig` shape — server reads these fields and calls
`CreateSAMLProviderConfig` / `UpdateSAMLProviderConfig` against
Firebase Auth on Update.

`rp_entity_id` and `callback_url` are output-only — the server
derives them from the org's resource name and Firebase Auth's
hosted callback endpoint, respectively.

name.description:
The resource name of the SsoConfig. Format:
`organizations/{organization}/ssoConfig`.

firebaseProviderId.description:
Output only. The Firebase Auth provider id. Server-managed; the
server creates / updates the underlying Firebase provider config
when this SsoConfig is updated. Format: `oidc.<slug>` for OIDC,
`saml.<slug>` for SAML.

displayName.description:
Required. Human-readable display name shown on the sign-in
screen and in the Firebase console.

enabled.description:
Optional. Whether SSO is currently active. When `false`, the
SsoConfig remains stored but `auth:resolveProvider` returns
NOT_FOUND for the org's domains and no Firebase provider is
exposed.

oidc.description:
OIDC provider configuration. Set when the IDP supports OAuth
2.0 / OpenID Connect.

saml.description:
SAML 2.0 provider configuration. Set when the IDP only speaks
SAML.

createdBy.description: Output only. The identity that created this SSO config.

createTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when the SsoConfig was created.

updatedBy.description: Output only. The identity that last modified this SSO config.

updateTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when the SsoConfig was last modified.

etag.description:
Output only. A checksum computed by the server based on the
current value of the SsoConfig resource.

v1SsoConfig.description:
SsoConfig is the per-organization SSO/IDP configuration. AIP-156
singleton sub-resource of Organization — there is at most one
SsoConfig per org, addressable at `organizations/{org}/ssoConfig`.

Get/Update RPCs live on the Organizations service (this is the
resource definition and request shapes only). Phase 4 wires server-
side encryption: client_secret travels cleartext over TLS, the
server envelope-encrypts it via Cloud KMS before persisting.

Domain ↔ SsoConfig linkage is implicit: any of the org's `Domain`
resources in `state=VERIFIED` route to this SsoConfig when
`enabled=true`. There is at most one SsoConfig per org so the
mapping is unambiguous.

permissions.description:
The subset of `TestIamPermissionsRequest.permissions` that the
caller is allowed on the resource. Permissions not in this list
are denied (or unknown).

newOwner.description:
The user resource that now holds the `owner` role on the
organization. Format: `organizations/{organization}/users/{user}`.

previousOwner.description:
The user resource that previously held the `owner` role and was
demoted to `admin` as part of the transfer. Same format as
`new_owner`.

v1TransferOwnershipResponse.description:
Response message for `Organizations.TransferOwnership`. Returns the
before/after owner refs so clients can confirm the swap and
optimistically update their UI without a follow-up read of the
affected Member rows.
